SOTA models tested in EdotEnv environments show: (1) struggle with deep iteration on research ideas, (2) higher reasoning doesn't increase performance, (3) agents stop trading when losing instead of trading smarter
EdotEnv uses real-world market data (not synthetic) with verifiable, immediate rewards — no LLM judge or human expert needed

angles: EdotEnv's key insight: markets are the ideal continuously-evolving benchmark because they self-difficultate as models improve — unlike static benchmarks that saturate
The 'benchmaxxing' problem: traditional evals become meaningless for model comparison as they saturate; EdotEnv offers a dynamic alternative
Quant workflows as transferable research skills: feature engineering, backtesting, portfolio design, regime adaptation — all transferable to general ML research
The surprising finding that higher reasoning doesn't help in trading environments challenges assumptions about reasoning models
EdotEnv's approach to reward design: verifiable, immediate rewards from market outcomes instead of LLM judges or human evaluators
The stochasticity problem: market paths make comparability difficult — fixed-seed regimes vs. path stochasticity as a design choice
